task:
Make the stoker's handover fully automatic: when a stoker session has written, committed, pushed and verified its handover, the SAME `bin/stoker.sh` invocation must end that session and open a fresh one on its own. The operator must never type anything — not `/clear`, not a relaunch — as part of the handoff.

## Why (the operator's words, to be recorded verbatim)

The operator said, in this order:
1. "i want the handoff to happen without me having to do anything so figure out how to do that"
2. "the rule shouldnt say that. no rule should say that i would have to do anything manually as a part of the handoff"

Today `hooks/stop.py` ends with "Clear now with /clear; the next session starts from HANDOVER.md", `rules/global.md` says "Never open a successor session from a session that is ending; the operator opens it from the project", and `skills/handover/SKILL.md` has a section titled "The one part that is not automatic". All three contradict the operator's position and must change.

## Facts already established — do not re-research

- `/clear` sent from the Claude app to a `--remote-control` session is a known Claude Code bug: it shows "Context cleared" without clearing, and the app then hangs on "sending..." (github issues #68059, #62734). So `/clear` is NOT the mechanism. Do not build anything that depends on `/clear`.
- Hook output cannot type into the session, and injecting keystrokes into the terminal (TIOCSTI, tmux send-keys, osascript) is off the table: tmux is not installed, Homebrew is not installed, and keystroke injection is denied by the permission system. Do not attempt any of these.
- A process spawned from a hook is not guaranteed to outlive the `claude` process (issue #41577). So the relauncher must NOT be spawned by a hook; it must be the thing that launched `claude` in the first place.
- `claude --help` on this machine (2.1.272): `claude [options] [command] [prompt]` accepts an initial prompt as a positional argument; `--remote-control [name]` starts remote control with an optional name; `-n/--name <name>` sets a display name. Verify the exact spelling yourself before relying on it.
- The original reason for the "never open a successor" rule (commit 5da5b5a) was specific to opening a *cloud* session from inside a session: it arrives with no checkout. That reason still holds for the cloud tool, so keep the guard's denial of that tool. It does not apply to a local relaunch in the same folder.
- `hooks/session_end.py` documents that SessionEnd has a 1.5 s budget and cannot block termination, so nothing that matters may happen there.

## Design (build this; deviate only if you prove it cannot work, and report why)

1. **A supervisor owns the process lifecycle.** `bin/stoker.sh` becomes a thin entry point that execs `tools/stoker.py` (all logic in `tools/`, `bin/` holds only entry points — README says why). The supervisor:
   - launches `claude` as a child with inherited stdin/stdout/stderr (the operator sees exactly what they see today), with `HEATER_ROLE=stoker`, `--remote-control` named `heater stoker` (honour `HEATER_SESSION_NAME` as today), in the repository root;
   - passes an initial prompt on EVERY launch, because a fresh interactive `claude` otherwise sits idle forever with nobody to type. Something like: "You are the stoker. Run bin/bearings.py, read HANDOVER.md, and continue the work." Keep it short; `CLAUDE.md` and the SessionStart hook carry the rest;
   - watches for a **handover-complete marker file** (put it under whatever `hooks/heater_hook.py` already uses for per-session state; look at how `context.announced()` / `mark_announced()` store their mark and follow that pattern). When the marker appears, it ends the child gracefully (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a bounded wait), removes the marker, waits a couple of seconds, and launches a fresh `claude`;
   - exits the loop when `claude` exits on its own WITHOUT the marker (the operator typed `/exit` or Ctrl-C), so the operator can still stop the stoker. Exit with the child's exit code;
   - keeps a relaunch back-off so a `claude` that dies instantly on launch (bad auth, bad flag) cannot spin: after 3 consecutive launches that live under 30 s, stop and print why, on stderr, in plain words;
   - logs every launch, marker-triggered restart, and exit through the existing `log()` in `hooks/heater_hook.py` (or the equivalent in `tools/`), so `bin/bearings.py` could show it later. Do not extend bearings in this task.
2. **The Stop hook writes the marker instead of asking the operator.** In `hooks/stop.py`, the branch that today says "Clear now with /clear" must instead: write the marker, log `handover_complete`, and return a `say()` telling the model the session is ending and the supervisor is opening the successor. It must still only do this when `handover.problems(quick=True)` is empty — i.e. handover note current, tree clean, pushed. Never write the marker on a session that is not the stoker (`role(payload) != "stoker"`), and never twice (the marker's existence is the guard).
3. **`tools/handover.py`** stops printing "the operator opens it from the project"; print what actually happens now.
4. **`rules/global.md`, Sessions section.** Replace "Never open a successor session from a session that is ending; the operator opens it from the project." with one imperative bullet under fifty words that (a) keeps the ban on opening a successor from inside a session (the cloud-tool reason still stands and the guard still enforces it), and (b) names `bin/stoker.sh` as the thing that opens the successor. Also check whether "Archive a session once its handover note is pushed, never before." still reads correctly for a terminal session that the supervisor ends; if it needs an edit, keep it under fifty words. Run `tools/style_lint.py`. Record the REASON for the rule change in the commit message, never in the rule file.
5. **`OPINIONS.md`.** Append opinion 12, titled "The handoff needs nothing from me", carrying the two quotes above verbatim, in the operator's voice like opinion 11. Do not edit any other opinion.
6. **`skills/handover/SKILL.md`.** Rewrite "The one part that is not automatic" and "Do not open the next session from this one" to describe the supervisor. Keep the ban on seeding a cloud successor and its reason (no checkout). Rewrite step 6–7 of the Procedure accordingly ("Only then clear" and "say where the operator opens it" are both wrong now). Update `hooks/pre_tool_use.py`'s denial reason text at line ~112 if it quotes the old rule verbatim.
7. **`README.md`** command table: update the `bin/stoker.sh` line and the `bin/handover.py` lines to say what they do now.
8. **Tests.** Fix the tests that assert the old wording (`tests/test_handover.py:144`, `tests/test_guard.py:300`, `tests/test_stoker.py` around line 385). Add behavioural tests for the supervisor using a **stub `claude`** (a small script placed first on PATH by the test) that: records its argv and env to a file, then sleeps until signalled. Prove at least:
   - launch passes `HEATER_ROLE=stoker`, the remote-control name, and an initial prompt;
   - writing the marker ends the stub and a second stub launch follows, and the marker is gone before the second launch;
   - the stub exiting by itself without a marker ends the supervisor with the stub's exit code;
   - three instant deaths stop the supervisor with a plain-words message.
   And a test for `hooks/stop.py`: with a clean handover state and the stoker role, the hook writes the marker exactly once and never for a non-stoker role.
9. **Reversibility.** This change is reversible by `git revert` of its commit, and the operator's plain `claude` in the folder keeps working untouched throughout. State that in the commit message. Prove nothing destructive: the supervisor must never delete or rewrite anything but its own marker file.
10. **Deploy.** If `tools/deploy.py` links `bin/stoker.sh` or hook files anywhere, make sure the new `tools/stoker.py` needs no extra deploy step (it is reached through the repo path). Run `bin/deploy.py --check` and report the result.

## What is out of scope

- Do not touch pokerbot or any pokerbot dispatch.
- Do not change the 30%/45% marks or `tools/context.py`.
- Do not try to make the Claude app follow the new session automatically; whether the app needs one tap to open the successor is unknown and will be observed on the first real handoff. Say so in the commit message so the next session knows to watch for it.

## Done looks like

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` green, `bin/gate.sh` exit 0, `bin/deploy.py --check` reports in sync (or names exactly what drifted and why), the six files above changed, the branch pushed, and your report naming: every file changed, the exact rule text you wrote, the exact `claude` command line the supervisor runs, and the one thing you could not prove without a live interactive session.
done_when: Suite green, gate exit 0, deploy --check in sync, supervisor + stop-hook marker + rule/opinion/skill/README rewrites landed on a pushed branch, report names the rule text and the exact claude command line.
